newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - ITALY - TUESDAY, JULY 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - ITALY - TUESDAY, JULY 1.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italy's cross-party reform commission completed work on re-writing the constitution and sent its recommendations to parliament where they are likely to be met with a barrage of amendments. The package, which envisages a radical shake-up of the country's electoral laws, was approved by a big majority (all).
* The Italian Treasury said it will pay another 3.875 trillion lire to state industrial holding IRI for the last part of the purchase of telecommunication group STET (all).

* Gianni Agnelli, honorary chairman of industrial giant Fiat, said the question of who will succeed Cesare Romiti as chairman of the group will not be resolved until next year, adding that he knew who it will be but he did not want to tell reporters. Agnelli also said that Europe's car industry, like the sector worldwide, faced significant overproduction and manufacturers were unlikely to make global alliances in the next few years (all).
* Giancarlo Cimoli, managing director of state-run rail company Ferrovie dello Stato, said the railway giant lost 3.84 trillion lire in 1996, around one trillion more than forecasted (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi, speaking three days after the Bank of Italy cut the official discount rate, said that there was a need for further cuts (La Repubblica).
* National statistics office Istat said Italian gross domestic product (GDP) fell by 0.4 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997 (Sole 24 Ore).
* State-controlled energy group ENI opened 2.39 percent up at 9,800 lire per share in Milan after the end of its public share offer (OPV) on Friday. The shares ended 0.40 percent up (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
